summary: A Kubernetes-native DBaaS control plane built around intent + reconciliation, with all mutations modeled as durable, idempotent operations in a strongly consistent metadata Postgres. The data plane uses Patroni (K8s Leases) for HA and WAL-G/pgBackRest to object storage for backups/PITR, with versioned, roll-forward routing configs consumed by routers and explicit restore-to-new-cluster cutover.
strengths: Production-grade control-plane patterns: async ops, idempotency keys, optimistic concurrency, per-cluster admission/locking, and append-only versioned routing
Solid safety/ops story for HA and PITR: readiness gates before routing activation, manifest/checksum tracking, and explicit PITR health window computation
weaknesses: Scaling risks at stated fleet size: per-shard K8s objects (StatefulSets/Services/Leases/Jobs) and router polling/refresh against the metadata DB can become operationally and performance heavy without more hierarchy/caching/fanout control

Missing/under-specified hard parts: multi-region/DR and metadata DB failure strategy, stronger fencing guarantees under K8s API partitions, and concrete resharding/migration mechanisms (online key moves, transactional semantics, rollback)
